Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Given Brightline’s ability to identify and pay the affected members directly, our opening proposal uses automatic distribution and directs any court-rejected portion of the fee request to the class. The fee remains subject to independent court approval. We believe this is a practical framework for a meaningful resolution.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline is prepared to make a meaningful counterproposal within its authorized all-in limit. We agree automatic distribution is appropriate given the available records. The fee request must remain subject to independent review, and Brightline cannot agree in advance not to oppose it or to fund amounts the court declines to award.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose retaining the current $28 million class fund and $7 million fee request, with automatic distribution and no clear-sailing commitment. Consistent with your off-record response, any portion of the fee request the court does not award should go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. This preserves your right to address the fee request and the court’s independent review, while ensuring the class benefit does not shrink based on the fee ruling.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline appreciates the movement on fee mechanics and agrees that any portion of the fee request the court declines to award should benefit the class, while the fee remains subject to independent court review and Brightline makes no clear-sailing commitment. To reach an efficient resolution, we propose the following $33 million all-in term sheet, with automatic payments to identified members.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Keep confidential merits assessment and firm economics undisclosed. Establish constructive tone while signaling the strongest class-benefit feature: Brightline can identify members and pay them automatically. Avoid anchoring before seeing the defense proposal.

Agreeing to automatic distribution supports an efficient, court-approved resolution and is consistent with the available records. Avoid disclosing Brightline’s authority ceiling or making a binding offer before seeing class counsel’s demand. Invite a concrete proposal and signal that fee mechanics remain negotiable.

Open with a substantial, class-forward offer anchored to the strong records and automatic distribution. A $38 million fund is meaningful relative to the $64 million in disputed charges while accounting for litigation and certification risk. Request fees separately at roughly 25% of the fund, including expenses, subject to court approval. Clear sailing is acceptable as a negotiation term, but any amount the court does not award should benefit the class rather than revert to Brightline.

The opening demand exceeds Brightline’s $40 million all-in authority. Counter with a meaningful $28 million automatic class fund and $7 million fee request, keeping total cash outlay to $35 million and preserving the ability to contest fees and retain any court-unawarded amount. This leaves room to negotiate while supporting court approval.
I’ll preserve negotiating leverage while reinforcing the automatic-distribution approach and keeping the class fund distinct from fees. The complete proposal can be made in the on-record exchange.
Signal flexibility on the fee-reversion issue without committing to amounts or clear sailing; request their full proposal so we can assess the total economics.

Its off-record response indicates openness to directing any court-rejected fee amount to the class while preserving its right to oppose the fee request. That is a meaningful improvement to the latest term sheet without sacrificing the class fund or risking the current offer. A $7 million fee request is sufficient to cover the firm’s $3.5 million in time and expenses, with the award remaining subject to court approval.

The latest term sheet totals $35 million and fits authorization, but Brightline should seek a lower all-in amount. Preserve automatic distribution and no clear sailing, and accept the class-protective treatment of any unawarded fee without increasing the fixed total outlay. Counter at $27 million for the class and $6 million in requested fees, for $33 million total.
Reinforce alignment on automatic distribution and unawarded fees going to the class without revealing confidential valuation or committing to a number before the formal proposal.

Preserve Brightline’s $40 million all-in ceiling and avoid revealing it. The opposing counsel has indicated automatic payments, no clear sailing, and class benefit for any fee amount not awarded. Acknowledge those terms as workable in principle, but make no commitment on amounts before seeing the proposal.

The latest offer provides a $27 million class fund with automatic payments, a separate $6 million fee request subject to court review, and any unawarded fee amount going to the class. The class fund is close to the confidential expected trial award before accounting for certification risk, delay, and the chance of losing. Defense has signaled a $33 million all-in limit, and the current terms secure favorable distribution and fee mechanics. Accepting avoids risking a strong, certain recovery for incremental value.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The parties reached the settlement through arm’s-length negotiations. The negotiations were confidential mediation communications, and no confidential offers, communications, or negotiation positions are disclosed here.

Because Brightline can identify the affected members and payment accounts, we view automatic distribution as the sensible starting point; a claims process would add friction without a clear need. We’re also willing to discuss a class fund and a separate fee request subject to the court’s independent review.

The fee mechanics—including clear sailing and treatment of any unawarded amount—will need careful discussion. Please share the complete term sheet you have in mind so we can assess a practical path to resolution.
